subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget, tombstone/supersede, and conflict resolution across memory plugins?
rationale: The gap is real, but the correct fix depends on durable storage, privacy, rollback, review UX, plugin API, and migration choices that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

options.title: Limit V1 To Memory-Core
options.body: Implement only bundled memory-core CLI and SQLite behavior now, accepting that external memory plugins need a later compatibility/API alignment step.

options.title: Defer Lifecycle MVP
options.body: Keep current search, promotion, and dreaming behavior while concrete stale-memory symptoms stay tracked separately until lifecycle work becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle memory-plugin API and storage semantics, then split implementation into schema, provenance, write-path, and operator-surface PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage/schema and current memory surface history make him the best available routing candidate for lifecycle contract direction.
